content.title: About
content.content: A vanilla ice cream sandwich consists of two soft waffle cookies with creamy vanilla ice cream sandwiched between them. It is a popular snack often sold in packs of 2–4 pieces.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first ice cream sandwich appeared in the United States in the 1960s as a convenient summer treat.
Vanilla is considered the most neutral flavor and is often used as a base for adding various fillings and toppings.
The waffle cookies are usually made without added sugar to let the ice cream’s sweetness shine.
Ice cream sandwiches are commonly packaged in individual boxes, making them ideal for vending machines and street kiosks.

items.title: Source of calcium
items.content: Vanilla ice cream contains dairy, which provides calcium important for bones and teeth.

items.title: Quick energy source
items.content: The sandwich delivers fast energy through carbohydrates from the cookies and sugar in the ice cream, useful during active days.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Dairy ingredients and a small amount of egg in the cookie batter supply vitamins B2 and B12.

items.title: Milk and gluten allergy
items.content: The sandwich contains milk and wheat flour, which can trigger reactions in people with those allergies.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Sugar in the ice cream and cookies makes the product calorie‑dense; people with diabetes should limit consumption.

items.title: Melting at high temperatures
items.content: Storing above ‑ 18 °C causes the ice cream to melt quickly, which can lead to bacterial growth.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The sandwich can be eaten straight from the package after a quick chill in the freezer. Optionally, slice it and add fresh berries, nuts, or chocolate sauce.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep frozen at ‑ 18 °C or lower. Once removed from the package, it should be consumed within 30 minutes to prevent melting.
